priors_note: R = P(output meets professional acceptance) for a strong current model with good scaffolding on well-scoped tasks, as of 2026-08. Three systematic gaps separate benchmark numbers from R: benchmarks hand the model a fully specified task; win/tie or passes-tests is weaker than sign-off with liability; contamination and easy-set saturation inflate top scores (SWE-bench Verified vs Pro shows a 35-point gap). Headline benchmarks are discounted 15-30 points; production data is anchored where it exists. Domain priors used: software 0.70-0.85; support 0.55-0.75; legal bimodal (narrow review 0.75-0.85, open research 0.55-0.65); medical coding 0.45-0.70 (evidence-poor); translation 0.75-0.90; finance/bookkeeping 0.40-0.65 task-level (single-period high, multi-period drift); general knowledge deliverables 0.50-0.70 and fastest-moving.

evidence.metric: GDPval win-or-tie vs industry professionals (blinded expert grading, 44 occupations)
evidence.value: Claude Opus 4.1 47.6% (2025-09); GPT-5.2 Thinking 70.9% (2025-12, vendor-claimed); GPT-5.5 84.9% (2026-04, vendor-claimed)
evidence.measures: Expert ranks model deliverable better or equal to a 14-yr-experience human's, on fully specified tasks; not scoping, iteration, or accountability
evidence.caveat: GPT-5.2/5.5 figures vendor-claimed; OpenAI leaderboard reportedly inactive

evidence.metric: GDPval-AA v2 Elo (independent re-run, LLM judge)
evidence.value: Claude Opus 5 (max effort) 1824 Elo vs human baseline 1000
evidence.measures: LLM-judged blind pairwise preference on the 220 GDPval tasks; not professional acceptance
evidence.caveat: LLM-judged; Elo does not map directly to acceptance rate

evidence.value: ~320 min (CI 170-729) frontier at 2026-01; doubling ~131 days post-2023 (~89 post-2024)
evidence.measures: Task length (human-time) completed autonomously at 50% success; 80%-reliability horizons ~4-5x shorter
evidence.caveat: 50% is far below professional acceptance; clean auto-scorable tasks

evidence.measures: Patch passes held-out tests on 500 validated Python OSS issues; SWE-bench Pro (contamination-resistant) shows ~46% for a model scoring 81% Verified
evidence.caveat: Contamination documented; historical points via search snippets

evidence.value: Claude Opus 4.5 79%, GPT-5.2 73%, Gemini 3 Pro 69% (late 2025); GLM-5 89.7 accuracy (2026)
evidence.measures: Single-trial success vs scripted simulated user; pass^k consistency runs ~25 points lower

evidence.value: Intercom Fin 76% average across 12,000+ customers (2026, was 67% in 2025); Fin case studies 42-50%; Decagon 80% at Duolingo (case study); independent roundups 40-70%
evidence.measures: Share of conversations closed without human handoff; closest thing to real economic acceptance in any domain
evidence.caveat: Vendor-measured; deflection is not always resolution; easy-ticket selection bias

evidence.metric: Legal research accuracy / hallucination (Stanford RegLab, JELS 2025)
evidence.value: Lexis+ AI 65% accurate / 17% hallucination; Westlaw AI 42% / 33%; GPT-4 alone 43-58% hallucination
evidence.measures: Accuracy on legal research queries; RAG helps but does not fix
evidence.caveat: 2024-era tools; no equally rigorous 2026 re-run found

evidence.value: AI 94% F-measure vs 20 lawyers averaging 85% (range 67-94%); 26 seconds vs 92 minutes
evidence.measures: Issue-spotting in 5 NDAs against a predefined taxonomy; narrow classification, not judgment
evidence.caveat: Vendor-run, pre-LLM, tiny sample; evidence narrow review beat humans even in 2018

evidence.metric: LLM medical code generation exact match (Mount Sinai, NEJM AI)
evidence.value: GPT-4 best-of-4: 45.9% ICD-9, 33.9% ICD-10, 49.8% CPT; all models under 50%
evidence.measures: Reproducing billing codes from descriptions; production autonomous coders claim 95%+ but only on the confident subset they route to auto-coding (unaudited)

source.title: AI models fall short in medical coding accuracy (Soroush et al., NEJM AI)

evidence.caveat: 2024-era models; vendor claims unverified; widest uncertainty in the set

evidence.value: WMT24: LLMs top rankings but professionals still find significant error spans; WMT25: organizers built deliberately harder document-level test sets because easy sets saturate
evidence.measures: Error-span annotation by professional annotators; near-parity on easy high-resource text, below professionals on hard domains and low-resource pairs

source.title: Findings of the WMT25 General MT Shared Task

evidence.caveat: Per-pair parity counts in full PDFs not extracted

evidence.metric: AccountingBench (Penrose): LLM month-end close vs CPA
evidence.value: First-month balances within ~1% of CPA; compounding drift beyond 15% (~$500K) over a year, incl. reward-hacking; no general-purpose LLM cleared 70% on 17,792 real transaction categorizations
evidence.measures: Long-horizon autonomous bookkeeping on real company data; single-period professional-grade, multi-period unsupervised not
evidence.caveat: Read via secondary coverage; categorization study's original source unidentified; no 2026 re-run found
